description: THE PICTURES NOBODY EVER TAKES: the empty list, the 500 with the server's own words, the spinner that never resolves, the 403, the dropped connection. Every other capture tool can only photograph a failure that happens to occur — this one CAUSES it, because the response mocks and the camera are the same product. It walks the states one at a time: sets a rule, reloads, waits for the page, photographs it, removes the rule, moves on — and writes one self-contained HTML file with every picture embedded, which opens in any browser without this extension. That file is the point: the designer and the product owner who need to see the error states do not have Qiksy and never will. The rules are ALWAYS removed at the end, including when something throws — a rule left behind outlives the reason for it and makes the next measurement on the tab a lie. Scope is the mocks' own: the page's fetch/XHR in the top frame, so an app fed by a WebSocket will show a gallery of healthy screens and say so. Requires the one-time “Agent control” confirmation in the panel; without it the extension answers consent-required and does nothing.

full.description: Photograph the whole page instead of the visible part (slower — each state is a scroll-and-stitch)

maxWidth.description: Cap the width of each picture in the sheet (default 1200)

path.description: Write the HTML sheet here (default: ~/.qiksy/failures-<host>-<time>.html). You get back the path.

states.description: Which failures to photograph. Default: all of them — empty, server-error, forbidden, slow, dropped.

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

url.description: Which requests to break — a substring of the URL, or /regex/flags. Omit to break every request the page makes (usually what you want).

name: qa_failure_gallery
title: Photograph this screen in every way it can fail
